name: Post-flush stabilization entry (15m long, break-even + partial TP)
rationale: MECHANISM (H4 with a break-even-after-first-TP exit): the basing entry is confirmed-exhaustion, but the V can still fail on a second leg down; taking a partial profit and moving the stop to break-even once the first leg fills frees the runner to ride the recovery risk-free — the asymmetric structure a confirmed-base long deserves. Counterparty: late dip-sellers after forced flow exhausts. Entry: open_interest below a floor (flush occurred) AND range_position cross_up through a low floor (off lows) AND rsi cross_up through an oversold-exit level (curling up) AND vol_realized below a ceiling. Exit: a first partial-TP leg, then break-even on the runner with a trailing distance. DISCONFIRMER: ablate against H1 on the same sample — no tail/maxDD improvement means the wait is pure lag; range_position cross_up alone matching means generic bottom-fishing. The partial/BE structure must not merely mask a negative-edge core — the base spec must beat buy-and-hold net of fees.
catalyst: post-flush base entered with a partial-TP + break-even runner to ride a risk-free recovery
